rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.3-2.5 and 3, own SWAT model of the Lower Mekong driven by TRMM/GPM precipitation and GLDAS temperature, calibrated (2005-2006) and validated (2001-2004, 2007-2015) against observed daily/monthly discharge at six gauges. Q2: Section 3.2 and Figs 3-5, the satellite-forced model explains about 84% of daily streamflow variance in calibration, monthly NSE 0.86-0.95 in validation, captures timing of onset and end of seasonal (flood-season) flow; Section 3.3 and Fig. 10, flood duration (days above flood threshold) computed from observed and simulated discharge, e.g. Mukdahan 2011. Q6: Section 2.1 and Table 2, results reported for the whole Lower Mekong Basin at sub-basin outlets up to Kratie (656,518 km2). Q7: Section 3.2, authors found that running the model without adjusting the remote sensing precipitation overestimates streamflow by about 13%, so a separate precipitation correction factor per sub-basin was required. Q8: Discussion, model results are uncertain due to errors in input data, parameters and process representation; comparison based on monthly flows so aggregation may mask individual event prediction; Section 3.2, model slightly off in some peak flow estimates.
rows.notes: Support for the claim is indirect: remote sensing precipitation drives a validated streamflow model, but the study does not test prediction of extreme-event timing/intensity as such; flood duration and predictability (Colwell index) results under changed upstream inflows are hypothetical scenario outputs not checked against observations, and peak flows were acknowledged to be slightly off. Q3: only one method (model vs gauge comparison). Q4: no intermediate variable isolated beyond the streamflow output. Q5: six nested sub-basins along one river in three countries, not treated as distinct regions/soils/climates. Q9: NSE and percent error are validation errors; SUFI2 used but no uncertainty bands or dispersion reported for the result.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, own SWAT model runs with satellite forcing, calibrated and validated against observed Lower Mekong discharge.
rows.notes: The study does not report any result on allocating water resources more efficiently or on water conservation; it quantifies streamflow variability, predictability, flow reversals, 7-day maxima and flood duration under hypothetical <U+00B1>30% upstream inflow scenarios and states that such results can guide decision makers. Providing streamflow information is at most a precondition for improved allocation.

notes: Full text appears complete, including appendices on dams, the nasaaccess tool and flow-regime metrics.
